Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that both ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) and ileorectal anastomosis are used to treat intra-abdominal desmoid disease. However, there is no conclusive evidence suggesting that these two surgical approaches have different outcomes for patients with desmoid disease.

The fact that the morbidity associated with desmoid tumors has not been shown to differ between IPAA and ileorectal anastomosis implies that both approaches may be effective in managing this condition. In contrast, the results of the previous question suggest that desmoid tumors arising after restorative proctocolectomy have similar outcomes, regardless of whether they occur after IPAA or ileorectal anastomosis.

Therefore, it can be concluded that the surgical approach for intra-abdominal desmoid disease may not differ between patients with an ileal pouch and those with an ileorectal anastomosis. Further studies are needed to confirm this finding and to better understand the outcomes of these surgical approaches in different patient populations.
